$comment: sc-22738. The ONE declaration of the per-lane default anchor composition. Read by scripts/memory-calibration-harness.mjs (ANCHOR_STRATEGY, which planAnchor applies to any plan row carrying no `strategy` override) AND by crates/sceneworks-worker/src/inference_runtime.rs (every_planned_lane_row_resolves_a_weights_free_contract_implementing_its_rung, via include_str!). Both sides used to spell it out independently and nothing bound them; changing a rung here now reds the Rust test unless the contracts follow. This is the LAW's composition, not an operator knob — see the ANCHOR_STRATEGY doc comment for why, and for the single per-row escape.

enginesThatAlwaysStage.$comment: SW-F363. Providers whose generator stages EVERY request (text encoder, then DiT, then VAE, each released before the next maps) whatever rung is selected, so their least-optimized achievable anchor is the STAGED composition and a `:resident` regime row would claim a render that cannot happen. Read by scripts/memory-calibration-harness.mjs (validatePlan: such a provider's rows engage staged_residency and plan no `:resident` row) and by crates/sceneworks-worker/src/inference_runtime.rs (the staged override is legitimate for these; on MLX each listed provider's registered descriptor must carry `unconditionally_engages_staged_residency`). Evidence at the pin: mlx-gen-minimax-h3 h3_image/model.rs sets `unconditionally_engages_staged_residency: true`. The Candle lane lists nothing: candle-gen-minimax-h3 image_model.rs keeps the text encoder, DiT and VAE decoder warm on a resident request whenever its warm estimate fits the device, so a resident render can happen there.
